 Hon'Ble Kshitij Shailendra, J.

1 .  Heard Shri Lalit Kumar Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State-opposite party No. 1 and Shri Krishna Kumar Shukla, learned counsel for opposite party No. 2, who has filed vakalatnama today in Court, which is taken on record.

2. The present application under Section 528 BNSS has been filed by the applicant for quashing the impugned charge sheet dated 29.12.2023, cognizance/summoning order dated 10.05.2024,
non-bailable warrant dated 07.08.2025 as well as entire proceedings of Criminal Case No. 6445 of 2024 (State vs. Arvind Goel) arising out of Case Crime No. 417 of 2023, under Sections 420, 406 and 504 IPC, Police Station Kotwali, District Bareilly pending in the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Bareilly.

3. Apart from challenging the proceedings on merits, submission has been made that the dispute between the parties was in relation to business transactions and during the course of time, they have amicably settled their dispute and a written compromise on Rs.90/- non-judicial e-stamp paper has been executed on 07.08.2025 in District Court, Bareilly.
According to the said compromise, the parties have agreed for not proceeding with the said criminal case.
The original compromise dated 07.08.2025 is on record.
The same bears signatures of the parties as well as witnesses and also photographs of the parties to the dispute.

4. Learned counsel for opposite party No. 2 submits that based upon the compromise, his client does not propose to prosecute the applicant and, therefore, he has no objection if the present application is allowed.

5. Considering the submissions made and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gian Singh v. State of Punjab and Another (2012) 10 SCC 303 as well as Nikhil Merchant vs Central Bureau of Investigation, 2008 (9) SCC 677, the prayer made deserves to be allowed.
